title: From Billion-Scale to Million-Scale Language Models: Operational Capabilities for Embedded Post-Exploitation
abstract: arXiv:2610.23534v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for resource-constrained environments due to their low computational footprint. These characteristics also make them candidates for future autonomous malware, where connectivity, latency, privacy, or operational constraints may preclude cloud-based inference. Yet the ability of ultra-compact models to support malware during post-exploitation remains poorly understood.   We systematically evaluate seven open-source SLMs (20M-1.5B parameters) on two post-exploitation code-generation tasks: Directory Enumeration and Backdoor Generation. We compare Python (high-resource) and Lua (low-resource) across prompting strategies, task formulations, iterative reasoning, grammar-constrained decoding, and execution-feedback loops.   Results show that offensive code-generation capabilities do not increase linearly with model size. Successful execution depends on the interaction of model capacity

translated_title: 从十亿级到百万级语言模型：嵌入式后渗透利用的实战能力
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.23534v1 公告类型：交叉  摘要：小型语言模型（SLM）因其较低的计算资源占用，在资源受限的环境中越来越具有吸引力。这些特性也使其成为未来自主恶意软件的候选方案——在这类场景中，连接性、延迟、隐私或操作约束可能使基于云的推理无法实现。然而，超紧凑模型在后渗透利用阶段为恶意软件提供支持的能力仍然鲜为人知。我们系统地评估了七个开源小型语言模型（2000万至15亿参数）在两个后渗透代码生成任务上的表现：目录枚举和后门生成。我们比较了Python（高资源语言）和Lua（低资源语言），涵盖多种提示策略、任务表述方式、迭代推理、语法约束解码以及执行反馈循环。结果表明，攻击性代码生成能力并不随模型规模的增大而线性提升。成功执行取决于模型容量
tldr: 该研究首次系统评估了七个开源小型语言模型（2000万-15亿参数）在后渗透恶意软件代码生成任务上的表现，发现攻击性代码生成能力并不随模型规模线性增长，而是取决于模型容量等多因素的交互作用。
en_tdlr: This study systematically evaluates seven open-source small language models (20M-1.5B parameters) on post-exploitation malware code-generation tasks, revealing that offensive code-generation capabilities do not scale linearly with model size but depend on the interplay of multiple factors including model capacity.
